== Biography ==
Thomas was born in 1863, probably in Gransha, Islandmagee, County Antrim, Ireland, the son of [[Ross-26224|James Ross]] and [[Dick-4754|Catherine Dick]]. He was baptised on 06-Nov-1863 in Islandmagee Methodist Church.

In 1891, Thomas married [[Ross-25889|Ann Jane ("Annie") Ross]] at the 1st Presbyterian Church in Larne, County Antrim. He was recorded as full age, a Bachelor and a farmer residing in Gransha, Islandmagee. Annie was recorded as full age, and a spinster residing in Walbrook Cottage, Islandmagee. Unfortunately their Father's names were reversed on their marriage record. Thomas' Father was James Ross (Farmer) and Annie's Father was John Ross (Mariner)<ref>Ireland Civil Registration Marriage Index https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1891/10666/5886623.pdf</ref>

During the 1901 Census of Ireland, Thomas and Annie were residing in a house 32 in Gransha (Islandmagee, Antrim) with their 4 sons.<ref>The National Archives of Ireland 1901 Census of Ireland http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Antrim/Islandmagee/Gransha/990088/</ref><ref>The National Archives of Ireland 1901 Census of Ireland Household Return Form http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/nai000359403/</ref>

Sarah was born about 1822 in Cookstown, County Tyrone. She is the daughter of [[McGeagh-14|John McGeagh]].  Her mother may have been Elizabeth McGuin or Elizabeth Rankin.

In 1847 she married Rev. William McCaw, originally from Cookstown but now a Presbyterian minister in Manchester, England<ref>"Ireland Civil Registration Indexes, 1845-1958," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FTB6-VPT : 10 March 2018), MARRIAGES entry for Sarah Mcgeagh; citing Cookstown, 1847, vol. 4, p. 219, General Registry, Custom House, Dublin; FHL microfilm 101,241.</ref> who would go on to be Moderator of the United Presbyterian Synod in 1883.<ref>https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/e9fad747-f86c-4d56-b20a-1df728690a00</ref>  They settled in Manchester where William was a Presbyterian minister.

By 1851 they had two children, Mary and William.<ref>"England and Wales Census, 1851," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:SG16-YZ3 : 11 September 2019), Sarah Mc Caw in household of William Mc Caw, Cheetham, Lancashire, England; citing Cheetham, Lancashire, England, p. 55, from "1851 England, Scotland and Wales census," database and images, findmypast (http://www.findmypast.com : n.d.); citing PRO HO 107, The National Archives of the UK, Kew, Surrey.</ref>  A third, Florence followed in 1862.  By 1871 they were also looking after their 8-year old niece, Sarah Dickson.<ref>"England and Wales Census, 1871", database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KDXM-XGB : 10 July 2021), Sarah McCaw in entry for Willm McCaw, 1871.</ref>

In 1861 William 39 from Ireland, a Presbyterian Minister, was living with his wife Sarah 39 from Ireland, and a daughter Mary aged 13, born Manchester, in Smedley Lane, Cheetham Hill, Manchester. <ref> "England and Wales Census, 1861", , FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M7NZ-H8P : Sat Mar 09 18:45:41 UTC 2024), Entry for William McCaw and Sarah McCaw, 1861. </ref> 

Sarah McCaw of Holly Lodge, died 12th February 1895, married aged 70, wife of a clergyman. Her son in law Isaac Stevenson, of 15 Myrtle Terrace registered the death. <ref>Londonderry SR District https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/deaths_returns/deaths_1895/05941/4687746.pdf (indexed as Sarah McGuran)</ref> She is  buried in Derry Cemetery. <ref>{{FindAGrave| 249336884}} </ref>

51179117.Name: Elder-7251
51179117.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

'''Robert Elder''' was born about 1831, probably in County Antrim. His birth estimate is based on his reported age of 40 at marriage.

On 14 June 1871 Robert married [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Glasgow]] in the Ballymoney registration district. The original register describes him as a 40-year-old bachelor and farmer and names his father as '''[[Elder-7300|Nathaniel Elder]], farmer'''. Mary was a 28-year-old spinster residing at Lisnagaver, daughter of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], farmer.<ref name="ElderGlasgow1871">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Robert Elder and Mary Glasgow, 14 June 1871; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1871/11341/8162804.pdf digital image].</ref>

The Lisnagaver valuation revision books later show Robert succeeding Alexander Glasgow as occupier of lot 25, containing 8 acres 2 roods 10 perches. This supports continuity between the marriage family and the Lisnagaver Glasgow household but does not by itself establish Robert’s death date.<ref name="LisnagaverRevision25">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, valuation revision books for Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, PRONI VAL/12/B/4/16C and VAL/12/B/4/16D, lot 25; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx PRONI search and image viewer].</ref>

=== Family and later records ===

The 1901 census records Robert's widow [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Elder]] at Gortahar with their children [[Elder-7302|Mary]], [[Elder-7303|Robert J.]] and [[Elder-7304|Jane M.]].<ref name="Census1901">1901 Census of Ireland, Gortahar, Rasharkin, County Antrim, Mary Elder household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPB2-KNM2 indexed record].</ref> In 1911 Robert J. headed the continuing household with his mother, sister Jane and nephew [[Elder-7305|Samuel Glasgow Elder]].<ref name="Census1911">1911 Census of Ireland, Gortahar, Rasharkin, County Antrim, Robert J. Elder household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QYHR-52T2 indexed record].</ref>

A published transcription of the First Garvagh Presbyterian register records the marriage of [[Elder-7301|William Elder]] and [[McMaster-2595|Ellen J. McMaster]] on 6 September 1864. William's father was [[Elder-7300|Nathaniel Elder]], farmer, and Robert Elder was a witness.<ref name="WilliamMarriage1864">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/GarvaghP1/Marriages/1845-1889marr.html First Garvagh Presbyterian Church marriages, 1845–1889], entry 110, William Elder and Ellen J. McMaster, 6 September 1864.</ref> The common father, occupation, locality and Robert's role as witness make William a likely brother, although the identification remains qualified pending the original register and further family evidence.

A Robert Elder aged 64 whose death was registered at Ballymoney in the fourth quarter of 1894 is a strong candidate for this man and would explain Mary's widowed status in 1901.<ref name="Death1894">Ireland civil registration death index, Robert Elder, Ballymoney, October–December 1894, vol. 1, p. 100; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FTZP-9M6 indexed record].</ref> The original death entry is required before the identification is treated as proved.

== Sources ==
<references />

44286694.Name: Glasgow-3167
44286694.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

'''Mary Glasgow''' was born about 1843, probably in County Antrim. Her birth estimate is based on her reported age of 28 at marriage.

On 14 June 1871 she married [[Elder-7251|Robert Elder]] in the Ballymoney registration district. The original register describes Mary as a 28-year-old spinster residing at Lisnagaver and explicitly names her father as [[Glasgow-951|“Alexr. Glasgow,” farmer]]. Robert was a 40-year-old bachelor and farmer, son of Nathaniel Elder.<ref name="ElderGlasgow1871">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Robert Elder and Mary Glasgow, 14 June 1871; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1871/11341/8162804.pdf digital image].</ref>

The valuation revision books provide independent locality evidence. Robert Elder later replaced Alexander Glasgow as occupier of Alexander’s Lisnagaver holding, lot 25, containing 8 acres 2 roods 10 perches.<ref name="LisnagaverRevision25">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, valuation revision books for Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, PRONI VAL/12/B/4/16C and VAL/12/B/4/16D, lot 25; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx PRONI search and image viewer].</ref>

Mary was present at Gortahar on 27 February 1892 when she registered the death of her mother, [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The death register identifies the informant as the deceased woman’s daughter, Mary Elder.<ref name="MaryGlasgowDeath1892">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Mary Glasgow, 27 February 1892, Gortahar; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1892/06049/4723532.pdf digital image].</ref> Mary Elder therefore died after that date.

=== Gortahar household ===

The 1901 census index records Mary Elder, aged 60, widowed, Presbyterian and a farmer, as head of a Gortahar household with children [[Elder-7302|Mary]], [[Elder-7303|Robert J.]] and [[Elder-7304|Jane M.]].<ref name="ElderCensus1901">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPB2-KNM2 FamilySearch, Ireland census index], Mary Elder household, Gortahar, County Antrim, 1901.</ref> In 1911 her son [[Elder-7303|Robert J. Elder]] headed the continuing Gortahar household with his widowed mother Mary, sister [[Elder-7304|Jane M. Elder]] and a two-year-old nephew displayed as “Samuel Glasgow.”<ref name="ElderCensus1911">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QYHR-52T2 FamilySearch, Ireland census index], Robert J. Elder household, Gortahar, 1911; individual entry for [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QYHG-YHMM Mary Elder].</ref>

The nephew was registered as '''[[Elder-7305|Samuel Glasgow Elder]]''' at Ballymoney in the third quarter of 1908; Glasgow was his middle name rather than his surname.<ref name="SamuelGlasgowElder1908">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FBP3-95M Ireland civil registration birth index], Samuel Glasgow Elder, Ballymoney, July–September 1908, vol. 1, p. 111.</ref> The continuing residence and relationships, together with Samuel's Glasgow middle name, make this household a high-confidence continuation of the family formed by Mary and Robert Elder. Samuel's parents remain unidentified.

A Robert Elder aged 64 whose death was registered at Ballymoney in the fourth quarter of 1894 is a strong candidate for Mary's husband and would explain her widowed status in 1901.<ref name="RobertElderDeath1894">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FTZP-9M6 Ireland civil registration death index], Robert Elder, Ballymoney, October–December 1894, vol. 1, p. 100.</ref> The original death entry is still required before the identification is treated as proved.

=== Disambiguation ===

This profile was previously identified with Maryan Glasgow, aged 17 in the 1851 Glenleslie household of [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]].<ref name="Glenleslie1851">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Glenleslie, Dunaghy, Kilconway, County Antrim, house 21, household of John Glasgow.</ref> The original 1871 marriage register instead says that Robert Elder’s wife was 28 and names her father as Alexander Glasgow. The Glenleslie Maryan should therefore not be used to assign this Mary a birth in 1834 or John Glasgow as grandfather.

A Mary Jane Elder died at Lisnagaver on 11 June 1897, aged 65, with John Elder, described as her son, as informant.<ref name="MaryElderDeath1897">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Mary Jane Elder, 11 June 1897, Lisnagaver; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1897/05858/4660280.pdf digital image].</ref> That age conflicts with Mary’s reported age at marriage, and the record has not been linked to Robert Elder’s family. It remains a same-name candidate rather than this profile’s death.

The former suggestion that she was [[Glasgow-2045|Mary Ann (Glasgow) Bell]] is also unsupported. No primary record found gives Robert Elder’s wife the middle name Ann.
A marriage for Mary Glasgow and Elder was registered on 14 June 1871 in the Magherafelt district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 14 June 1871, Magherafelt district, M/1871/N1/1863/1/179.</ref>

== Biography ==
=== Early Life in Illinois (1864–1890s) ===
Alexander C. Elder was born 6 February 1864 in Illinois, the son of Robert S. Elder and Nancy E. (Mary E.) Bruce. Alexander spent his childhood in Gallatin County, Illinois, first in Shawneetown (1870) and later in New Market Township (1880). His father, Robert S. Elder, was a Kentucky‑born farmer, and the family maintained strong ties to both Illinois and western Kentucky. By 1880, Alexander, age 17, was working on the family farm.
The Elder household was large, with at least nine children, and census records show a stable farming operation with both parents present.

==== Siblings ====
(As enumerated in the 1870 and 1880 Illinois censuses)
* A.F. Elder (b. c.1858)
* E.F. Elder (b. c.1859)
* B.F. Elder (b. c.1861)
* V.L. Elder (b. c.1866)
* M.M. Elder (b. c.1868)
* V.O. Elder (b. c.1865–1866)
* L.M. Elder (b. c.1871)
* G.R. Elder (b. c.1874)
These siblings form a large, mobile Elder household typical of post–Civil War Illinois river communities.

=== Migration to Kentucky & Marriage (1890s) ===
Sometime in the early 1890s, Alexander migrated to Crittenden County, Kentucky, likely following kin networks or agricultural opportunity. His marriage to Lena Clare Elder on 6 February 1895 in Crittenden County, Kentucky placed him within the Elder community centered around Marion and Crayne.

By 1900, Alexander and Lena were living on West Main Street in Marion, renting a farm property and raising their first two daughters. Two elderly women—Mary E. Elder (73) and Mary D. Elder—lived with them, identified as “aunts,” suggesting extended Elder kinship support.

This marriage united two Elder lines long established in the county—Alexander descended from the Scottish-Protestant Elder line originating in Spartanburg, South Carolina, and Lena from the Maryland Catholic Elder line through William Elder and Elizabeth Finch.

==== Children ====
(As confirmed by census and Find A Grave)
* Elva Myrtle Elder (1896–1918) – married Roberts
* Mina Wheeler Elder (1899–1914)
* Florence Cordova “Dova” Elder (1901–after 1940) – married Edward Tabor
* Elmer Stinson Elder (1904–1976)
These four children appear consistently across the 1900–1950 census series in the household of their widowed mother.

=== Occupation ===
Farmer  
Alexander is consistently listed as a farmer, both in Illinois (family farm) and Kentucky (head of household, 1900). His work was typical of smallholder agricultural families in Crittenden County at the turn of the century.

=== Death ===
Died: 1906, Crittenden County, Kentucky
Burial: Elder Cemetery, Crittenden County
Find A Grave Memorial: 68066714
Alexander’s death left Lena a widow with four children under age ten. She appears as a widowed head of household in the 1910 census, confirming his death occurred between 1900 and 1910, with 1906 supported by cemetery records.

=== Early Life (1875–1895) ===
Lena spent her childhood in the household of her grandparents, J.C.J. Elder and Mary Ann Pierce Elder, in Marion, Crittenden County. The 1880 census records her as age four, a granddaughter, living among a cluster of Elder aunts and uncles. Her upbringing in this extended household shaped the intergenerational living patterns she later maintained as an adult.

==== Parents ====
Although her 1880 census entry lists her as a granddaughter in the household of J.C.J. Elder (John Calvin Jackson Elder) and Mary Ann (Pierce) Elder, multiple compiled genealogies and later census records identify her mother as:
* Mother: Mary Eunicy (Eunice) Elder (born Kentucky)
* Father: Unknown / not recorded in surviving civil records
Lena consistently reports both parents born in Kentucky.
Her placement in her grandparents’ household in 1880 suggests she was raised primarily by them.

=== Married Years (1895–1904) ===
After marrying Alexander C. Elder on 6 February 1895, Lena settled on West Main Street in Marion. By 1900, the couple had two daughters—Eva Myrtle and Mina—and shared their home with Alexander’s elderly mother, Mary E. Elder, reinforcing the Elder tradition of multigenerational households.
Alexander died 1906, leaving Lena a widow with four young children.

This marriage united two Elder lines long established in the county—Alexander descended from the Scottish-Protestant Elder line originating in Spartanburg, South Carolina, and Lena from the Maryland Catholic Elder line through William Elder and Elizabeth Finch.

==== Children ====
Lena was the mother of four children, all of whom survived to adulthood according to the 1910 census, though two died young
* Elva Myrtle Elder (1896–1918) – married Roberts; died at age 22
* Mina Wheeler Elder (1899–1914) – died at age 15
* Dora / Cordova “Dova” Elder (1901–after 1940) – married Edward Tabor
* Elmer Stinson Elder (1904–1976)
These children appear consistently across the 1900–1950 census series.

=== Widowhood & Household Head (1904–1960) ===
==== 1910 ====
Lena appears as head of household, age 34, widowed, supporting her family as a washerwoman on her own account. She owned her home free of mortgage, a significant achievement for a young widow. Her household included all four children and two elderly women—Mary Pierce (83) and Mary Elder (54)—likely her grandmother and mother.
==== 1920 ====
Lena is listed as a farmer, operating her own general farm. Her daughter Dova and son Elmer remain at home, along with her mother Mary E. Elder.
==== 1930 ====
Still head of household, Lena lives on a farm with:
Elmer S. Elder, son; Mary E. Elder, mother; Cordova (Dova) Tabor, daughter; Edward C. Tabor and Wilma J. Tabor, grandchildren
==== 1940 ====
Lena resides with her son Elmer, his wife Ruth, and several extended relatives on Kid Ridge Road. She reports a 5th‑grade education and no income, relying on household support.
==== 1950 ====
At age 74, Lena continues to live with her son Elmer’s family on a farm outside Marion. She is listed as “Keeping House”, no longer working for wages.

=== Death & Burial ===
Died: 12 May 1960, Crittenden County, Kentucky
Age: 84
Burial: Mapleview Cemetery, Marion, Crittenden County
Plot: Section B & C
Find A Grave Memorial: 53578970
